newsitem.title: UK: From the Flightdeck - The Air Cargo Week in Review.
newsitem.headline: From the Flightdeck - The Air Cargo Week in Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the global air cargo industry in the week September 2 - September 6.
**SEPTEMBER 2**
AUCKLAND - Analysts and brokers say Air New Zealand faces challenges ahead after announcing a 13.4 percent decline in earnings to NZ$225.5 million in the year ending June, 1996.
WELLINGTON - The New Zealand government approves an application by Air New Zealand to lift the limits on foreign shareholding in the national flag carrier from 35 percent to 49 percent.
LONDON - The Climate Action Network says air travel could be the prerogative of the rich if environmentalist plans to protect the skies from pollution are successful.
CANBERRA - Qantas and Japan Airlines propose to re-arrange and codeshare their flights from Queensland to Tokyo, subject to Australian government approval.
HELSINKI - Finnair says its passenger load factor fell 1.4 percentage points year-on-year to 76.4 percent in July.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa says it is being probed by the German cartel office over its pricing structure on domestic routes.
LONG BEACH, California - Polar Air Cargo says it has been tentatively-awarded a new U.S. - Japan freighter route by the U.S. government.
WINNIPEG - A local consortium says its plan to launch a global air service for freight forwarders has advanced to the stage of securing aircraft and financing, for a launch next May or June.
ZAGREB - Croatia Airlines says it is launching 12 scheduled flights to the Bosnian capital Sarajevo this month.
FARNBOROUGH, England - McDonnell Douglas says it had six firm orders for new planes from four airlines companies.
* McDonnell Douglas chairman Harry Stonecipher says its 1996 full year earnings were set to meet analysts forecasts and would be sharply up on two years ago.
BRISBANE - New Zealand airline operator Kiwi International says it has won a Queensland Supreme Court order allowing its stranded A320 Airbus aicraft to return to regular services.
BRUSSELS - AEA says global freight traffic carried by Western European airlines in July 1996 was up 3.2 percent on the same month last year to 1.95 billion FTK's.
* AEA says global freight traffic carried by Western European airlines in the first seven months of 1996 was up 3.7 percent on the same period last year to 13,29 billion FTK's.
LONDON - Defence secretary Michael Portillo says Britain will go ahead with the 40 billion pound Eurofighter advanced combat jet.
* Portillo says Britain is prepared to buy 232, Eurofighter 2000 fighter aircraft.
STOCKHOLM - Sweden's civil aviation authority Luftfartsverket says air passenger volumes increased by five percent in the first half of 1996 to 8.6 million passengers.

FARNBOROUGH - A senior member of the four-nation consortium says Europe's Airbus Industrie is likely to offer a one-third share in its new A3XX superjumbo plane to foreign firms to help finance the project.
FRANKFURT - Condor Flugdiens, the charter carrier of Lufthansa says it planned to place confirmed orders for 12 Boeing 757-300s.
VIENNA - Tyrolean Airways, majority owned by Austrian Airlines, says it will invest up to 800 million Schillings until the end of the year to expand its fleet of regional aircraft.

BASLE - Airport authority figures show global traffic handled at Basle-Mulhouse-Freiburg airport in the first seven months of 1996 totalled 50,834 tonnes, a 14 percent rise on the same period last year.
LONDON - Statistics from the Hong Kong civil aviation department show total air cargo handled in June rose 5.3 percent against the same period last year.
FARNBOROUGH - A company spokesman says British Aerospace Plc is set to announce a new deal leasing up to eight turboprop aircraft to a Spainish regional carrier.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa Cargo says it will raise ex-Germany air cargo rates by up to 10 percent on selected routes from October 1.

FARNBOROUGH - Senior industry officials say British Aerospace hopes consolidation in the European defence and aerospace industries will see its own identity dissolved in a series of cross-border mergers by 2002.

FRANKFURT - A spokesman for the high court in Frankfurt says four suspects have been released from detention in an investigation into alleged corruption during the construction of Frankfurt airport's second terminal.
SAO PAULO - Federal authority Infraero says Brazil's president Fernado Henrigue Cardoso was scheduled to inaugurate a new central wing at International airport complex in the capital Brasillia.
LONDON - Lufthansa UK cargo manager Bob Bingley says it will raise ex-UK air cargo rates to Tokyo and Seoul from October 1.

MADRID - Spainish independent carrier Spainair says it will inaugurate scheduled services from Madrid to Bilbao and Madrid to Malaga this winter, increasing the number of routes where it competes directly with state-owned Iberia.
FRANKFURT - The federal transport ministry says the German government has approved a bill to put a new air accord between Germany and Zimbabwe into German Law.

LONDON - UK-based Coyne Aviation says the UK government will ask the International Civil Aviation authority to investigate the seizure of a Cyone chartered Ilyushin-76 freighter aircraft by Ukraine customs on August 20.
BRUSSELS - AEA says global freight traffic shipped by Western European airlines on all-cargo aircraft rose by 1.7 percentage points in July 1996, compared to the same period 1995.
* AEA says the percentage of global freight traffic shipped by Western European airlines on all-cargo aircraft rose by 2.2 percentage points in the first seven months of 1996 on 1995 levels.
GENEVA - IATA says that London's key position as a world airline hub could be threatened by a British government decision to impose more stringent airport noise controls.
WELLINGTON - Air New Zealand managing director Jim McCrea says he expects the purchase of half of Australia's Ansett from TNT to be earnings positive in 12 months time.
GUADALAJARA, Mexico - An industry spokesman says drought-stricken Mexico will have to increase soybean imports to 2.6 million tonnes after its worst harvest in history.
**SEPTEMBER 3**

WASHINGTON - Bill White, deputy director of FAA's flight standards service, says it grounded the Miami-based carrier Rich International Airlines because of discrepancies in crew training, maintenance and equipment records.
JAKARTA - State-owned Antara news agency says Indonesia will comply fully with IACO safety standards to prevent a possible ban on Indonesian aircraft flying to the U.S.
SINGAPORE - The European Airbus Consortium says it has sold or agreed to sell a series of aircraft for delivery between 1998 and 2000.
* Condor airlines is to purchase 12 A320 passenger aircraft with an option for another 12 aircraft.
* Federal Express has ordered 11 additional A300-600 freighter aircraft for delivery between 1998 and 2000.
* A separate Airbus statement says Cathay Pacific has signed a contract to purchase three more ultra long-range A340-300s.
LONDON - Traders say shares in BAA tumbled to a one-month low amid concern that renewed hostilities in Iraq will hurt its core businesses.
FRANKFURT - Singapore Airlines says it will follow the lead of Lufthansa Cargo and raise ex-Germany rates to Singapore this autumn.
CANBERRA - Australian finance minister John Fahey says the government will call for tenders this month for three of the airports it plans to privatise.
LONDON - Britain says the Western allies are to extend the no-fly zone over southern Iraq to bring it closer to the capital Baghdad.
FRANKFURT - A spokeswoman for Condor denies reports that the airline has bought 12 Airbus A320 aircraft.
LONDON - BA chief executive Robert Ayling says that he expects significant progress in the stalled "open skies" aviation talks between the U.S. and Britain this month.
BRUSSELS - AEA says Western European airlines posted a 4.8 percent growth in passenger traffic year-on-year in July, down from the eight percent average monthly mark registered so far in 1996.
BRUSSELS - AEA says Western European airlines faced more delays in the second quarter of 1996 compared to the same time last year, with 17.4 percent of flights delayed more than 15 minutes.
